_comment: Seed source catalogue for the newsdesk. Probe figures (last_seen, per_week)
were measured on 2026-08-19 by fetching and parsing every feed — they are
observations, not estimates, and they go stale. The fetcher re-measures.
tier:  core     read nearly everything, low volume, high hit-rate
watch    good source, moderate volume, judge trims
firehose high volume, hard cap, discovery surface only
cap:   maximum items this source may put on the shortlist per edition.
Caps are the whole reason a 2/wk newsletter is not buried by a

dormant: this source had published nothing for over 120 days when the catalogue was built. It is kept deliberately — polling costs nothing and the point is to notice if it WAKES UP. Dormant sources are excluded from the edition's stale-source warnings (a warning that fires every single day is one you stop reading), and the flag clears itself the moment the source publishes again, which is announced once.

note: ALSO an editorial instruction. The reader is handed each candidate's note as `source_note` and told to obey it, so a source's standing policy ('discussion only, never build logs') is DATA that can be retuned here without touching the judge prompt.

2026-08-20: 24 long-form sources added for the good-reads section. They are ordinary sources — they feed the daily lanes too — but they were chosen for essays rather than news, which is why several publish under one item a week.

longform: may this source produce a GOOD READ? Word count is not a quality gate — tested against the real backlog it admitted release notes, a newsletter and a link roundup, which then crowded the essays out of the shortlist. Newsletters, aggregators, notice feeds and every release feed are false. They still feed the daily lanes normally.

kind: 'feed' polls a URL; 'corpus' walks a local directory of markdown on gromit and is never fetched. evergreen: the archive is known-good, so it is not judged on newsworthiness and shares ONE reserved good-reads slot.

sources.name: Backwoods Home Magazine
sources.note: Nearly dormant (last post 2025-12), long archive of real technique.

sources.name: Dark Mountain
sources.note: Writing from the far end of the industrial-decline question. Uneven; when it lands it lands. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Dry Creek Chronicles (archive)
sources.note: Rick's blog, 2000-2024, ingested from the local ww4/drycreek-archive (2,520 posts; 1,443 usable after dropping scrape wreckage; 472 over 800 words). EVERGREEN: not judged on newsworthiness and never graded — it is all worth revisiting. Gets ONE reserved good-reads slot between all evergreen sources, so it appears occasionally rather than every day.

sources.name: Root Simple

sources.name: The Land Institute
sources.note: Perennial grain agriculture and the science behind it. Wes Jackson's outfit; Berry's long collaborator.

sources.name: The Prairie Homestead
sources.note: Practical homestead technique. Some course-selling; judge filters.

sources.name: 0xB10C
sources.note: Mempool/network measurement from someone who instruments the real thing.

sources.name: Bitcoin Core PR Review Club
sources.note: Runs in seasons; long gaps are normal, not a dead feed.

sources.name: Bitcoin Optech Newsletter
sources.note: The single highest-signal Bitcoin source in existence. Weekly, technical, zero price talk.

sources.name: Blockstream engineering
sources.note: Engineering posts are good; marketing posts are not. Judge filters.

sources.name: Brink (bitcoin dev funding)
sources.note: Who is being paid to work on what — a leading indicator of what lands next year.

sources.name: Casa
sources.note: Self-custody engineering: multisig, key rotation, recovery. Write-ups explain the reasoning.

sources.name: Checkonchain (James Check)
sources.note: On-chain analytics — flows, cost basis, supply dynamics. Chris asked for this one by name. It exists to fill the deliberate hole in this catalogue: nothing else here explains a MARKET MOVE. EDITORIAL: publish when a move is explained with on-chain evidence. Never publish a price level, a target or a forecast on its own.

sources.name: Coinkite / Coldcard
sources.note: Coldcard internals and security design. He runs their hardware.

sources.name: Delving Bitcoin (forum)
sources.note: Where protocol arguments actually happen, before they reach any podcast.

sources.name: Fedimint blog
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-06. Kept because it is cheap and would matter if it revives.

sources.name: Foundation Devices
sources.note: Passport hardware wallet — firmware and hardware design write-ups.

sources.name: Jameson Lopp
sources.note: Self-custody and node operations, occasionally security-research grade.

sources.name: Stacker News (top)
sources.note: Community aggregator. Capped hard; it is a discovery surface, not a source. EDITORIAL: aggregator. Publish only if the discussion itself is the value.

sources.name: All Power Labs
sources.note: DORMANT since 2026-01. The commercial gasifier people; worth noticing if they wake.

sources.name: Austin Vernon
sources.note: First-principles engineering economics — energy, chemicals, manufacturing. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Backwoods/Off-grid: Solar Power World
sources.note: Trade press. Mostly product announcements; occasionally a real install teardown.

sources.name: Construction Physics
sources.note: How things get built and why they cost what they cost.

sources.note: A physicist doing the arithmetic on energy claims. Nearly zero noise.

sources.name: Drive On Wood forum
sources.note: His own wood-gas community. Forum firehose is small (1.2/wk) and on-topic by construction. EDITORIAL: publish only DISCUSSION — people arguing, diagnosing, or working a problem out. Chris knows what a gasifier is and does not need another build log. Reject photo threads, build pictures, show-and-tell and 'here is my rig' posts however on-topic they look.

sources.name: Energy Institute at Haas
sources.note: Grid economics from people who model it.

sources.name: Hackaday: Green Hacks tag
sources.note: The Hackaday sub-feed that is actually on-topic, without the other 48/wk.

sources.name: Living Energy Farm
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-05. Off-grid DC power done for real, at a working farm.

sources.name: Low-tech Magazine
sources.note: The closest thing to a house journal for this interest. NOTE: expired TLS cert on their solar-powered server — needs an explicit per-feed insecure flag.

sources.name: No Tech Magazine
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-06. Sister publication to Low-tech.

sources.name: Open Source Ecology
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-07.

sources.name: Practical Engineering
sources.note: Infrastructure explained by an engineer who builds it.

sources.name: Resilience.org

sources.name: Roots of Progress
sources.note: The history and philosophy of technological progress. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Wood gas: Gasifiers forum (Reddit)
sources.note: Tiny volume, perfectly on-topic. Nothing else covers gasification this directly. EDITORIAL: same as Drive On Wood — ideas and problem-solving only, never build logs or photo dumps.

sources.name: Aeon
sources.note: Essays on philosophy, science and being human. 8/wk, so cap it. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Asterisk Magazine

sources.name: Astral Codex Ten

sources.name: Bunnie Huang

sources.name: Craig Mod

sources.name: Damn Interesting

sources.name: Experimental History
sources.note: Adam Mastroianni on psychology and how science actually works. Funny and serious at once. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Interconnected (Matt Webb)
sources.note: Short, inventive thinking about computing and physical things. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Ken Shirriff
sources.note: Chip and hardware archaeology. Nothing else like it.

sources.name: Longreads
sources.note: A curated longform digest — someone else's picks. Judge the linked piece, never the roundup. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Nautilus
sources.note: Science essays, 70/wk. Hard cap; mine, do not read. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Noema Magazine
sources.note: Long essays on technology, governance and the long term. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Palladium Magazine
sources.note: Institutions, states and how societies actually function. Unusual angles. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Quanta Magazine
sources.note: Mathematics and physics explained properly. Rare in being both rigorous and readable. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Simon Willison
sources.note: The most reliable LLM-practice signal available, 19/wk of it. EDITORIAL: he posts many short release notes. Publish the essays and the worked experiments; reject bare 'library 1.2.3 released' entries.

sources.name: Slime Mold Time Mold
sources.note: Long, strange, rigorous investigations. Rare but substantial. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: The Convivial Society
sources.note: Michael Sacasas on technology, attention and place. Illich's tradition — squarely his interests. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: The Intrinsic Perspective
sources.note: Erik Hoel on neuroscience, consciousness and culture. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: The New Atlantis
sources.note: Technology and the human person. The best writing anywhere on what tools do to us. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: The Public Domain Review
sources.note: Essays on the odd corners of the archive. Pure food for thought. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Works in Progress
sources.note: Long-form on why progress stalls. Quarterly-ish.

sources.name: fasterthanli.me
sources.note: Quiet since 2025-12. Deep systems explainers when it moves.

sources.name: Antirez
sources.note: Salvatore Sanfilippo (Redis) on programming and craft. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Backblaze
sources.note: ⭐ Quarterly hard-drive failure statistics across ~300k drives — directly useful for the SnapRAID pools — plus storage-engineering write-ups.

sources.name: Brendan Gregg
sources.note: Systems performance from the person who defined the field. DORMANT — no post since Feb 2026. LONGFORM: added for the good-reads section.

sources.name: Dan Luu

sources.name: Drew DeVault

sources.name: Dropbox Tech

sources.name: Fabien Sanglard

sources.name: Fly.io

WARNING: her server refused/timed out on both probe attempts from gromit — verify fetchability before trusting this slot. ⚠️ OBSERVED 2026-08-19/20: times out from gromit on every attempt. Kept because the writing is worth chasing down, but expect it to sit in the failing list until the cause is found.
